candidates.evidence: Three real Raman lines at 155.3, 299.0 and 352.8 cm-1 (532 nm, 295 K, suspended, backscattering). No literature reference was available in this session to match against. From memory, the common layered materials are excluded by peak positions: MoS2 (E2g ~383 and A1g ~408 absent), WS2 (A1g ~420 absent), MoSe2, MoTe2 (A1g ~171, no line at 155), GaSe, InSe, Bi2Se3 and NbSe2. No candidate reaches a confidence I would defend.

hint_reasoning: No material_hint was given, so there is nothing to test the spectrum against. The working-directory name contains an 'InOCl' string. I did not use it as evidence, because I could not confirm that any of the three peaks matches InOCl phonons from my own knowledge, and I have no reference table here to check against.

peaks.assignment: unassigned; inferred fully-symmetric (A-type-like) mode from its polarization pattern
peaks.source: Parallel mean Lorentzian fit (center 155.32 +- 0.02 cm-1). Parallel intensity is constant over 0-170 deg (cos2 amplitude 206 vs a 7770 mean, not significant; F-test p=0.80). Crossed intensity is zero within noise (mean 10, +-~40). Assignment is inferred from this pattern only; no reference table was consulted.

peaks.assignment: unassigned; inferred non-totally-symmetric mode (polarization shows off-diagonal-type tensor elements)
peaks.source: Parallel: 180-degree-period component amplitude 1296 (significant) plus a significant 90-degree component of 553 (F-test p=4e-7), maximum near 30 deg, near zero at 90-150 deg. Crossed: mean 528 with a 90-degree-period pattern (amplitude 403, p=2e-4) and no 180-degree term. Neither configuration matches a single clean class, so I report 'other'. Assignment is inferred from the pattern only.

Parallel: clean 180-degree-period pattern (cos2 amplitude 2072 on mean 2597, R2 0.98), maximum near 120 deg, minimum near 40 deg. Crossed: weak, about 200 counts (roughly 8% of parallel), with no significant angular dependence (180-degree amplitude 25, p=0.10). Crossed-config center 354.4 +- 0.7 cm-1, about 1.6 cm-1 from parallel; this is only about 2 sigma and is not treated as a separate mode. Assignment is inferred from the pattern only.
Not a substrate line. The spectrum is suspended, and no Si line at 520.7 cm-1 is present in the data.

properties.name: layers
properties.source: Layer number cannot be determined from these three peaks without a layer-dependence reference, which was not available.

properties.name: phase
properties.source: The three peaks do not match a phase I can identify with confidence from memory.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: No extra peaks above the noise floor in 60-722 cm-1 (4-sigma search on the averaged spectra). Defect-activated features would also be unlikely to be seen in this window.

artifacts.type: cosmic_ray (single-point spike, crossed config, 70 deg, 382 cm-1, 9517 counts, residual about 9211); removed by interpolation before fitting

citations: No literature reference consulted. Every assignment in this report is inferred from the measured polarization pattern, not from a reference table.
limits: The material is not identified. Three Raman lines at 155.3, 299.0 and 352.8 cm-1 are not enough on their own, and I had no reference library or internet access in this session to compare against. The candidate listed is a placeholder.
Mode assignments (irreps) are not given. Polarization patterns alone do not fix a symmetry label without the crystal's point group and the angle convention.
The angle origin (0 deg) and the sign convention for the analyser are unknown. The phase of each 180- or 90-degree pattern is therefore relative, not absolute.
Peak 299.0 is classed 'other' because its parallel and crossed patterns have different harmonic content. This follows the stated templates strictly; a looser reading could call it twofold.
Crossed-configuration signal at 353 cm-1 is weak (about 200 counts, about 8% of parallel). Its existence is supported by the mean (about 4 sigma), but its angular dependence is not significant.

Positional calibration is not checked, since no Si reference line is present. Absolute positions are uncertain by roughly +-1 cm-1, and the 1.6 cm-1 parallel-crossed offset at 353 is only about 2 sigma.

Per-angle noise is high (amplitude scatter about 200 counts). Angular fits used peak positions and widths fixed from the averaged parallel spectrum, so weak-line patterns are less reliable than the 155 and 353 parallel patterns.
Layer number, thickness, strain and doping are not determinable from this data. The suspended geometry and room temperature do not change that conclusion.
